experiment: Social interaction lifecycle hooks (start, store_result_for_outcome, complete, cancel) and outcome-triggered banter

key_mechanism_findings.finding: Passive conversation containers vs. concrete social mixers
key_mechanism_findings.detail: sim_Chat (13998, display_name 0x482BA41C 'Chat with {1.SimFirstName}') and sim_BeAffectionate (13991, display_name 0xDB04B08F 'Chat') are passive SocialSuperInteraction containers that hold Sims in a conversation group. Earlier start-hook runs treated the internal name 'sim_BeAffectionate' as an affectionate action even at romance=0. Filtering passive containers and resolving STBL display names eliminates that false positive.

key_mechanism_findings.finding: Outcome decision timing precedes animation completion by several seconds
key_mechanism_findings.detail: In live Banter Lab traces, store_result_for_outcome fired 30-37 ms after _trigger_interaction_start_event on social mixers (for example, mixer_social_RespectfulIntroduction_greetings: start at +0.000s, outcome SUCCESS at +0.030s, complete at +2.390s; mixer_social_DiscussLocalFishingSpots: start at +0.000s, outcome SUCCESS at +0.037s, displayed reply at +3.175s, complete at +7.619s). Triggering generation at store_result_for_outcome supplies the verified OutcomeResult (SUCCESS or FAILURE) while still delivering dialogue mid-animation.
Interaction.cancel recorded live cancellation events with finishing_type='DISPLACED' when mixer_social_DiscussLogicalPuzzles_targeted_Friendly_alwaysOn_skills ended as the conversation transitioned.

outcome_comparison_samples.text:
Mortimer: Boo! I was going for ominous.
Alex: You startled me into noticing that crooked picture. Fix it.

Mortimer: A successful scare, and you’re still grading the décor. Impressive.
Alex: I’m rattled, not blind. That frame’s begging to be straightened.

live_in_game_exchanges.text:
Liberty: Hi, I’m Liberty. Nice to meet you—sorry, I nearly introduced myself to that lamp.
Alex: Alex. Nice to meet you too. The lamp seems neat, at least.

Liberty: There’s a good fishing spot nearby—quiet, scenic, and only mildly threatening to my balance.
Alex: I’m in. I’ll bring a tidy tackle box; you can keep an eye on the scenery.

Liberty: Logic puzzles are fun because every clue fits somewhere. Unlike my feet, apparently.
Alex: You’re good at them. And I can keep the pieces in a neat little pile.

limits: Not every interaction uses test-based outcomes; some greetings use InteractionOutcomeSingle, and some reaction super-interactions lack a display_name string ID.
High-autonomy rejection outcomes depend on Sim mood and relationship state unless forced or triggered by player-chosen risky socials.
